Ezer the Horite
EE-zer
proper noun
Hebrew etser, “treasure” or “store,” the name of a son of Seir the Horite and a duke of that people, distinct from other men called Ezer.

Biblical Definition

Ezer was a son of Seir the Horite, named among the sons who inhabited the land of Seir before the children of Esau came to dwell there (Gen 36:21). He is reckoned one of the dukes of the Horites, the chieftains of the children of Seir in the land of Edom (Gen 36:30). The Scripture sets down his children: “Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan” (Gen 36:27). This Ezer of Seir is to be distinguished from other men of the same name in the sacred record — an Ezer of the tribe of Ephraim, and Ezers among the builders and singers of the later books — for the name “treasure” was a common one in Israel and beyond. The chronicler gathered the Horite line again into his book of generations (1Ch 1:38,42). Ezer belonged to that ancient people whom the LORD planted in Mount Seir and afterward dispossessed, giving the land to Esau (Deu 2:22). The dictionary records him to witness that the LORD treasures up the names of the chieftains of the earth, even of a people now passed away. His name means treasure, yet his store and his dukedom are long gone; and the reader may learn that the only abiding treasure is laid up where moth and rust do not corrupt, in the inheritance reserved by the God who keeps the bounds of every habitation.

EZER, a son of Seir the Horite, named among the inhabitants of the land of Seir.

He is reckoned one of the dukes of the Horites in the land of Edom.

His sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.

He is to be distinguished from other men of the name Ezer in the sacred record.

His name witnesses to the God who treasures the names of the chieftains of the earth.

Key Scripture

Gen 36:21 — "And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom."

Gen 36:27 — "The children of Ezer are these; Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan."

Deu 2:22 — "As he did to the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, when he destroyed the Horims from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even unto this day:"

Gen 14:6 — "And the Horites in their mount Seir, unto Elparan, which is by the wilderness."

Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; he witnesses to the God who treasures the names of the chieftains of the earth.

expand to see more

Ezer is a name among the dukes of the Horites, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine him. The dictionary records him, and marks him from the other men called Ezer, that the reader who meets his name among the sons of Seir may know which man is meant and own him for a real duke of a real people.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the sovereign providence of God over the rise and fall of peoples, and the truth that the only abiding treasure is laid up with Him. He who planted the Horites in Mount Seir and afterward removed them hath determined the bounds of every habitation (Act 17:26), and keeps the inheritance of His own beyond the reach of decay.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “treasure” or “store,” this entry marks a son of Seir and a duke of the Horites.

Usage

"Ezer’s name means treasure, yet his store is gone; only the riches laid up with God endure."

"The LORD who knew the dukes of the Horites treasures the name of every one of His own."

"Let the reader lay up treasure where moth and rust corrupt not, in the keeping of the God who abideth for ever."
